faq.q: What comparison options can I toggle?
faq.a: Ignore case, ignore whitespace, ignore blank lines, trim trailing whitespace, and word/character-level highlighting. These affect only the comparison — the display keeps your original text. It uses a real LCS (longest common subsequence) line diff, and within changed lines it highlights the specific words that were added or removed in green and red.

faq.q: What's the difference between the side-by-side and unified views?
faq.a: Side-by-side shows Original and Modified in two columns with their own line numbers. Unified is the git-style view with - for removed and + for added lines in one column. Both show a stats bar (added, removed, changed, unchanged and a percentage-similar figure), and Prev/Next buttons jump between changes (keyboard n/p).

faq.q: Can I load files instead of pasting?
faq.a: Yes — drop a .txt or code file onto either side, or click to upload. Files over 5MB are refused as too slow to diff in a browser, and files that look binary (pdf, docx, images, zip, etc.) or contain too many replacement characters are rejected with a message telling you to paste the text. Very large pastes are capped at 6000 lines with a confirmation.

faq.q: How do I export the result?
faq.a: Copy a unified patch, copy either side on its own, download a .diff file, or export a ZIP bundle (via JSZip) containing changes.diff, an aligned side-by-side text view, original.txt, modified.txt and a README with the stats. Your two inputs are autosaved in your browser and restored next visit. Shortcuts: Ctrl/Cmd+Enter compares, s swaps.
